title: Reserve before you fill
description:
A vector that runs out of room allocates a bigger block, moves every element across and frees the old block. Filling a vector of a thousand strings one `push_back` at a time does that about eighteen times.

When you know how many elements are coming, say so first with `reserve`. Then there is exactly one allocation.

Fix `labels` so the vector it returns has room for exactly `count` elements and no more.
unitTests:
TEST("the contents are right") { const auto v{ labels(3) }; CHECK_EQ(v, (std::vector<std::string>{ "item 0", "item 1", "item 2" })); CHECK(labels(0).empty()); }
TEST("no room is wasted and nothing was regrown") { CHECK_EQ(labels(1000).capacity(), 1000u); CHECK_EQ(labels(37).capacity(), 37u); }
